result:
Reviewing the plan and tracing `write_tally_main` validation paths in the codebase.
schema_version	scope	severity	focus_area	location	what	scenario_or_breakage	suggested_fix
1	in_scope	important	correctness	plan.txt:39-55 / python/review_and_fix.py:841-877	The proposed `flush_review_batches` regression test does not require seeding a disallowed markdown header into artifacts that `_build_tally_body` actually reads.	With only valid `round-*/review-round-summary.md` files (`# Review Round N` plus `## Accepted Findings`), `_build_tally_body` produces bodies that pass `_validate_code_review_headers` today, so round-2 `flush_review_batches` can succeed on unfixed code and the new test would not fail red on the frozen-at-round-1 bug.	In the test, add a round-2 fixture that `_build_tally_body` copies verbatim, e.g. a `## Round 2` line in `round-2/review-round-summary.md` or accepted-finding prose, assert round-1 flush still writes `rounds == 1`, and assert round-2 flush updates `larch-logs/implement/<run_id>/code-review-tally.json` to `rounds == 2` with cumulative counts.
1	in_scope	important	correctness	plan.txt:34-35 / python/test_voting.py:555-581	Plan-review preservation is not actually asserted after the code-review gate change.	The combined `test_write_tally_header_validation_and_logger_kv_reemission` plan-review branch only checks exit code `0` and `LOG_WRITTEN=true`; it never loads the written `plan-review-tally.json` and checks that `body` is present. A regression that dropped plan-review `body` while keeping `write-tally` exit `0` would slip through.	After the plan-review `write-tally` call, read the batch file from the test log root and assert JSON `phase == "plan-review"`, `batch == "plan-review-tally"`, and non-empty `body` matching the input file.
1	out_of_scope	latent	code-quality	python/voting.py:816-823 / plan.txt:69-71	The plan makes every non-zero `_validate_code_review_headers` result non-fatal, including `rc == 3` read failures, not just `rc == 4` unrecognized headers that cause production `## Round 2` failures.	After `_validate_tally_args` has already verified the path is a non-symlink file, `rc == 3` is a rare TOCTOU/permission case; warning and writing anyway is broader than the reporting bug needs and weakens the only remaining body-file safety signal.	[SCOPE-REDUCTION] Keep the minimum fix to `rc == 4` (and any other future header-shape codes): warn via `_plain_diagnostic` and continue; leave `rc == 3` on the existing `_die` path unless a concrete failing run shows it on the hot path.
